bib.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

question: Which BERT pretraining design choices (masking, NSP, batch size, encoding, data size, training length) matter, and was BERT undertrained?
hypothesis: BERT was significantly undertrained and, with a better recipe, can match or exceed all post-BERT models.
contributions: A set of BERT design choices and training strategies that give better downstream performance
New dataset CC-NEWS; more pretraining data further improves downstream tasks
Shows MLM pretraining under the right design choices is competitive with other recent methods
Release of model, pretraining and finetuning code in PyTorch

method.summary: Replication study of BERT pretraining in fairseq: ablates masking, input format/NSP, batch size, byte-level BPE, data size and training length, then combines the best into RoBERTa and evaluates on GLUE, SQuAD and RACE.
method.task: masked language model pretraining, then finetuning on NLU tasks

datasets.name: CC-NEWS
datasets.size: 76GB after filtering; 63 million English news articles
datasets.source: English portion of CommonCrawl News, collected with news-please

datasets.name: OPENWEBTEXT
datasets.source: open recreation of WebText; Reddit-shared URLs with at least 3 upvotes

datasets.name: STORIES
datasets.source: Trinh and Le 2018, CommonCrawl subset filtered to Winograd-like style

datasets.name: GLUE (9 tasks)
datasets.split: dev for Sec 4 and single-task results; test via leaderboard

models.name: RoBERTa-large
models.init_from: random (GLUE RTE/STS/MRPC test: from MNLI model)

models.name: RoBERTa-base
models.params: inferred: 110M plus about 15M for larger vocab (Sec 4.4); not stated directly

models.name: BERT-base reimplementation (Sec 4 ablations)
models.tokenizer: BERT 30K character-level BPE in the original

training.objective: masked LM cross-entropy on 15% of tokens (80% [MASK], 10% unchanged, 10% random), dynamic masking regenerated each time a sequence is fed; no NSP
training.lr: peak 4e-4 (large), 6e-4 (base); 1e-4 / 7e-4 / 1e-3 for bsz 256 / 2K / 8K in Table 3 ablation
training.hardware: DGX-1 machines, 8x 32GB V100 GPUs each, Infiniband; 1024 V100 for the 100K-step run
training.compute: inferred: 1024 V100s for about one day for the 100K-step run; 500K-step runs not stated

other.static_vs_dynamic: original BERT duplicated data 10x for 40 epochs, each mask seen 4 times
other.finetune: RACE lr 1e-5 bsz 16 wd 0.1 4 epochs; SQuAD lr 1.5e-5 bsz 48 wd 0.01 2 epochs; GLUE lr {1e-5,2e-5,3e-5} bsz {16,32} wd 0.1 10 epochs; warmup ratio 0.06, linear decay (Table 10)
other.glue_test: ensembles of 5-7 models per task; RTE/STS/MRPC start from MNLI model; QNLI pairwise ranking; WNLI margin ranking loss with SuperGLUE format
other.racel: candidate+question+passage, [CLS] to FC layer, QA truncated at 128 tokens, total 512
other.squad2: binary answerable classifier trained jointly, losses summed
other.Adam_eps_note: training very sensitive to Adam epsilon; beta2 0.98 for stability with large batches

inference.samples: median of 5 seeds on dev; ensembles of 5-7 for test

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: MNLI-m, SST-2, RACE, per-task GLUE metrics

eval.protocol: Dev: median of 5 seeds, single task, no ensembling. Test: GLUE leaderboard ensembles; SQuAD 2.0 leaderboard; RACE test.

availability.data: CC-NEWS collected by authors; release not stated in text

limits: Data size and diversity are conflated (footnote 9).
Even the 500K-step model does not appear to overfit and would likely benefit from more training.
Architecture changes and larger models are left to future work.
Byte-level BPE vs character BPE comparison only from early experiments; slightly worse on some tasks.
Other methods (XLNet) might also improve with more tuning (footnote 2).
Possible that original BERT's no-NSP ablation kept the SEGMENT-PAIR input format (Sec 4.2).
Dev results use single-task finetuning; test GLUE uses task-specific tricks (QNLI ranking, WNLI), not comparable to BERT.
